title: Speedball
developer: The Bitmap Brothers; C64 conversion by Pantheon Software
build: Image Works disk, 1989 (C64 Preservation Project G64, speedball[mirrorsoft_1989](pal), SHA-256 57c5ad91...)

credits.role: music and sound effects (the game's credits)

accuracy.note: 60 of the 1,273 comments, checked by a fresh agent against the code; the eleven wrong and three others that said the same things were corrected

the pages' tests against the game's own routines: the tackle pairs (which pairs are never seen to touch) and the knockout (eight or ten wrong rounds) were miscounted in facts.md and on the Discoveries tab, and corrected

exclude: the loader's text screen, left as it was: spaces, then power-on bytes; the game never shows it

runtime: in play the two pitch screens ($6C00, $7400), the panel's screen ($7000) and the character set ($7800), all built from data held elsewhere ($DF55, $EC0D, the map at $F300); in the menus the bitmap at $6000
runtime: in play the pitch map, 40 columns by 74 rows, which pitch_map_build ($917D) writes; between matches it holds the play sprites, which play_sprites_in ($916A) copies to $5C00
include: the game's own data under the I/O chips, part of FILE1's copy at $C000-$FEFF: tile colours, menu blocks, text buffers, pitch pieces, the fonts and the character sets; the main code runs with all RAM ($01 = $30) and reads it there

io: the game runs with all RAM ($01 = $30, set at $20DC); the rows below are the stretches that bank the chips in
the launcher's colour flashes, between io_in and io_out
panel colours into colour RAM, between io_in and io_out
the raster interrupt and its slots, run with $01 = $0D
the music and sound calls, between io_in and io_out
the sprite registers for play, between io_in and io_out
the panel's colours into colour RAM, between io_in and io_out
colour_fill: colour RAM, between io_in and io_out
the prematch screen's colour RAM, between io_in and io_out
the menu screen's colour RAM, between io_in and io_out
panel_recolour: colour RAM, between io_in and io_out
box_colours: colour RAM, between io_in and io_out
the logo's colours into colour RAM, between io_in and io_out
the save and load code, which runs with the chips and the KERNAL in
the music driver, called with the chips in
